checks.detail: one-way ANOVA F of 24 h sequential offline gains 20.582; group effect F of the group x offline period ANOVA 14.541; group x offline period interaction F 3.382; Hedges' g of 24 h gains, children vs young adults 1.285; Hedges' g of 24 h gains, children vs older adults 2.449; Hedges' g of 24 h gains, adolescents vs older adults 1.256; Hedges' g of 24 h gains, young adults vs older adults 1.237

differences: Mean % of key presses excluded as RT outliers, Experiment 1: 1.79 here (children 2.05, adolescents 1.77, young adults 1.69, older adults 1.65) against 1.78 (2.03, 1.76, 1.68, 1.65) in the paper; Experiment 2 older adults: 1.35 against 1.34. The cause is not known: the flags here reproduce the authors' per-block RT means (source data) exactly for all 130 Experiment 1 participants.

Experiment 2, 24 h: for one child and one older adult the deposited session 3 files give other session 3 RTs than the authors' source data, so the 24 h statistics computed from this table differ from the paper: one-way ANOVA F of 24 h sequential offline gains 19.602 (paper 20.582); group effect F of the group x offline period ANOVA 14.307 (paper 14.541); group x offline period interaction F 3.668 (paper 3.382); Hedges' g of 24 h gains, children vs young adults 1.218 (paper 1.285); Hedges' g of 24 h gains, children vs older adults 2.202 (paper 2.449); Hedges' g of 24 h gains, adolescents vs older adults 1.231 (paper 1.256); Hedges' g of 24 h gains, young adults vs older adults 1.198 (paper 1.237). With the authors' source-data 24 h gains for those two participants, all seven values are reproduced; the 5 h statistics, which use sessions 1 and 2 only, are reproduced from the table.

In the authors' Experiment 2 source data the rows of five young adults are rotated by one participant (each row holds the next one's values); rows here follow the participant numbers of the data files, and the age and sex of these five come from the Table 2 sheet by participant number, so they may be affected in the same way.

The paper says 42 participants (16 children, 19 adolescents, 4 young adults, 3 older adults) took part in both experiments; the deposit has 39 participant numbers in both (14, 18, 4 and 3), whose Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 session 1 files are identical.

The paper says the third session of one young adult was missing; the deposit and the authors' source data hold all three sessions for every young adult (only one adolescent's session 3 random run is missing).
